title: Main theorem applied to tame types
body_html:
Main theorem applied to tame types

Theorem (synthesis). Let $G$ be a tamely ramified reductive group over a $p$-adic field with $p$ large enough, $\Sigma$ a Heisenberg–Weil datum with depth-zero Levi $M = G^{(0)}$. Then Main Theorem 8.2.1 gives $$\Rep_\Phi(G) \;\simeq\; \Rep_0(M).$$
proof_html:
All axioms required by Main Theorem 8.2.1 are verified for the tame Yu/AFMO datum:

Axiom Source
(K1)–(K3), (F1)–(F4) [[node:applications.tame_hypotheses_K]] (K3 via twisted-Levi tower)
(T1)–(T5), (E1)–(E3) [[node:applications.tame_T_axioms]]
(S) Hypothesis (S) for tame types via Bernstein + [KY]
(E4) Follows from Hom(κ_x, κ_y)_{K∩K} one-dim and G^{(0)}-trivial (proves (E3))
(K4) Standard via $K_x = G^{(0)}_{x, 0} J_x$
Global $\kappa$-extension Global β-extension existence (compatible κ-family on B(G_β)) (Skodlerack–Ye Thm 5.21, adapted to AFMO $\kappa_x$ via the Yu twisted-Levi reductive quotients of $\mathrm P^\circ(\Lambda_x)/\mathrm P_1(\Lambda_x)$)

With all hypotheses satisfied, [Sheaf7 Thm 8.2.1] applies directly. $\square$

Relation to other approaches

This is a sheaf-theoretic counterpart of the Hecke-algebra reduction in [AFMO2]. The key conceptual difference: our argument goes through equivariant coefficient systems on the generalized building $\BSigma$, whereas [AFMO2] manipulates Hecke algebras directly. The reduction of theta correspondence to the depth-zero case (via [LM]) is the originating motivation.

See Dat–Fintzen 2026: block decomposition + reduction to depth zero (tame) for a parallel approach via block decomposition.
